title: Game Dev with ADHD
author: AethericPulse
selftext: I'm developing my first game and running into a repeat pattern of getting to 80% and jumping to another task on repeat. Part of the reason is trying to maximise token usage and lack of time having a job and 7 month old. Was curious if anyone else runs into this pattern?

comments.author: candevor
comments.body:
All the time! I have so many projects and keep thinking about new ones. Some I keep going back to, some I never revisit. Tried doing projects so small that they can be done without me running out of steam, and it kind of works, but then the bigger projects (with more meaning/impact) are rarely completed. Some days I feel like getting somewhere, other times, totally disappointed. I am in the same boat with a full-time job, young children, and so many other things going on.  
How are you coping, and what do you think might help?

replies.author: AethericPulse
replies.body: Like I'm sticking to one specific project and trying to do as much as I can for it, but I'm not fully completing any segment. I do feel that I did enough to the point of doing full circle and now I'm back to tidy up some tasks but instead of finishing them one at a time, it's ending up with a bunch of them simultaneously 😅 it's kind of working but very stressful. More time and a holiday would definitely help.

replies.author: candevor
replies.body: I get you. Just saw your other comment about wanting to polish :D I think going with tiny/micro-game projects might help. Which you CAN polish and still finish in a week or even a weekend. Finishing something gives a great feeling, but as someone said below, players would enjoy a half-finished product if you set the right expectation and don't ask for too much money.

replies.author: AethericPulse
replies.body: My issue is I've nothing to show for it because of this process which is starting to make things difficult as I hit hurdles wrapping up tasks

comments.author: CzechYourStonks
comments.body: Same for me. I started many many projects and finished almost none. Some even generate money but I cannot make myself develop them further.

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
Its fine. As long as you have something playable, you can get somewhere 

Players prefer polished games but they are usually okay with 80% as long as they enjoy the experience

replies.author: AethericPulse
replies.body: I do really want to polish it and I will, I'm very peculiar about how I want things, but also need the dopamine from progress and with such little time daily, I don't make enough progress doing the final tweaks so end up doing different tasks

comments.author: icekiller333
comments.body: I found the best solution was to keep scaling down the scope of the game until I could finish it before getting bored and jumping to the next thing. It's taken a bunch of failures and abandoned demos before I got the gut feeling for whats in scope, but its super helpful now :)
